headline: For 165 million years, dinosaurs were the dominant life form on Earth
universal_truth: Even the mightiest can fall—dominance is always temporary
fun_facts: Dinosaurs ruled Earth for 165 million years; humans have existed for about 300,000 years
Birds are living dinosaurs—the only lineage that survived the mass extinction
Some dinosaurs were the size of chickens; others were longer than three school buses
discussion_questions: What can the rise and fall of dinosaurs teach us about power and permanence?
If dinosaurs hadn't gone extinct, would humans exist?
What might future beings discover about our civilization in fossils?

hook.script: For 165 million years, they ruled. From tiny feathered creatures to 100-foot giants, dinosaurs dominated every continent. Then, in geological instant, they were gone—except for one lineage that still soars overhead. Today, we enter the age of dinosaurs.

cliff.script: Dinosaurs survived for over 500 times longer than humans have existed. They weathered ice ages, volcanic eruptions, and continental shifts. So what could possibly end such a successful dynasty?
cliff.prompt: What ended the age of dinosaurs?

options.text: An asteroid impact triggered climate catastrophe 66 million years ago
options.response: Yes. A 6-mile-wide asteroid struck Mexico, causing global fires, then a years-long winter.

options.text: Gradual climate change made Earth uninhabitable for large reptiles
options.response: Climate change played a role, but the trigger was more sudden...

fact1.title: 165 Million Years
fact1.script: Dinosaurs appeared about 230 million years ago and dominated until 66 million years ago. That's 165 million years of rule. Humans have existed for about 300,000 years. If dinosaur history were a 24-hour day, human history would be less than 3 minutes.

fact2.title: The Survivors
fact2.script: Not all dinosaurs died. One lineage—small, feathered theropods—survived and evolved into birds. When you see a sparrow or a chicken, you're looking at a living dinosaur. The age of dinosaurs never truly ended; it just got smaller.

fact3.title: Incredible Diversity
fact3.script: Dinosaurs ranged from the 100-foot Argentinosaurus to the chicken-sized Microraptor. Some had armor, some had feathers, some had crests for display. They filled every ecological niche—just as mammals do today.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: 165 million years of dominance ended in a cosmic instant. Nothing—no matter how powerful—lasts forever. The dinosaurs remind us that adaptation matters more than size, and humility serves better than hubris.

outro.script: That's Day 51. Tomorrow, we'll peer inside a volcano. Until then, look at a bird—and see the dinosaur that lives on.

growTrack.title: Deep Time Perspective - See the Long View
growTrack.learning_objective: Develop perspective through geological time scales
growTrack.activity: Consider something that feels permanent in your life—a job, a relationship, an institution. Now imagine it from a 'dinosaur perspective': millions of years from now, what trace will it leave? How does this perspective change how you hold it?
